content.prompt:
The angle $\theta$ satisfies $\sin \theta = \frac{5}{13}$ and $\frac{\pi}{2} < \theta < \pi$.
What is the value of $\sin 2\theta$?

$\text{A. }\frac{10}{13}$
$\text{B. }-\frac{10}{13}$
$\text{C. }\frac{120}{169}$
$\text{D. }-\frac{120}{169}$

answer.worked:
We are given that $\sin \theta = \frac{5}{13}$ and $\frac{\pi}{2} < \theta < \pi$.
Since $\theta$ is in the second quadrant, $\cos \theta$ must be negative.
Using the Pythagorean identity $\cos^2 \theta = 1 - \sin^2 \theta$:
$$\begin{align*}
\cos^2 \theta &= 1 - \left(\frac{5}{13}\right)^2 \\
&= 1 - \frac{25}{169} \\
&= \frac{144}{169}
\end{align*}$$
Taking the negative square root for the second quadrant:
$$\cos \theta = -\frac{12}{13}$$
Now, use the double angle identity for sine:
$$\begin{align*}
\sin 2\theta &= 2 \sin \theta \cos \theta \\
&= 2 \left(\frac{5}{13}\right) \left(-\frac{12}{13}\right) \\
&= -\frac{120}{169}
\end{align*}$$
Correct answer: D.

$\textbf{(ii)}$ Suppose that $0<B<\frac{\pi}{2}$ and $B<A<\pi$.
Deduce that if $\tan A\tan B=-1$, then $A-B=\frac{\pi}{2}$.

answer.short: (i) $\cos(A-B)=\cos A\cos B(1+\tan A\tan B)$ is shown. (ii) If $\tan A\tan B=-1$, then $\cos(A-B)=0$ with $0<A-B<\pi$, so $A-B=\frac{\pi}{2}$.
answer.worked:
$\textbf{(i)}$
$$\begin{align*}
\cos(A-B) &= \cos A\cos B + \sin A\sin B \\
&= \cos A\cos B \left(1 + \frac{\sin A\sin B}{\cos A\cos B}\right) \\
&= \cos A\cos B (1 + \tan A\tan B)
\end{align*}$$

$\textbf{(ii)}$
If $\tan A\tan B = -1$, then $1 + \tan A\tan B = 0$.
Substituting this into the identity from (i):
$$\begin{align*}
\cos(A-B) &= \cos A\cos B (0) = 0
\end{align*}$$
Since $0 < B < \frac{\pi}{2}$ and $B < A < \pi$, we have $0 < A-B < \pi$.
The only value in the interval $(0, \pi)$ for which the cosine is $0$ is $\frac{\pi}{2}$.
$\therefore A-B = \frac{\pi}{2}$.

answer.worked: $$\begin{aligned}\mathrm{LHS}&=\frac{\sin2x\cos x}{\cos2x\sin x}\\&=\frac{2\sin x\cos^2x}{\cos2x\sin x}\\&=\frac{2\sin x\left(\frac12(1+\cos2x)\right)}{\cos2x\sin x}\\&=\frac{\sin x+\sin x\cos2x}{\cos2x\sin x}\\&=\frac1{\cos2x}+1\\&=\sec2x+1\\&=\mathrm{RHS}.\end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned}\mathrm{LHS}&=\frac{2\sin\theta\cos\theta-(1-2\sin^2\theta)+1}{2\sin\theta\cos\theta+(1-2\sin^2\theta)-1}\\&=\frac{2\sin\theta\cos\theta+2\sin^2\theta}{2\sin\theta\cos\theta-2\sin^2\theta}\\&=\frac{2\sin\theta(\cos\theta+\sin\theta)}{2\sin\theta(\cos\theta-\sin\theta)}\\&=\frac{\cos\theta+\sin\theta}{\cos\theta-\sin\theta}.\end{aligned}$$
Divide numerator and denominator by $\cos\theta$:
$$\begin{aligned}\mathrm{LHS}&=\frac{1+\tan\theta}{1-\tan\theta}.\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}\mathrm{RHS}&=\frac{\tan\theta+\tan\frac\pi4}{1-\tan\theta\tan\frac\pi4}\\&=\frac{\tan\theta+1}{1-\tan\theta}.\end{aligned}$$
Therefore $\mathrm{LHS}=\mathrm{RHS}$.

$$\begin{aligned}\mathrm{LHS}&=\frac1{\sin4A}+\frac{\cos4A}{\sin4A}\\&=\frac{1+2\cos^2(2A)-1}{2\sin2A\cos2A}\\&=\frac{\cos2A}{\sin2A}\\&=\frac{\cos^2A-\sin^2A}{2\sin A\cos A}.\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}\mathrm{RHS}&=\frac12\left(\frac{\cos A}{\sin A}-\frac{\sin A}{\cos A}\right)\\&=\frac12\left(\frac{\cos^2A-\sin^2A}{\sin A\cos A}\right)\\&=\frac{\cos^2A-\sin^2A}{2\sin A\cos A}.\end{aligned}$$
Therefore $\mathrm{LHS}=\mathrm{RHS}$.

Let \(A=\frac{5\theta}{7},\ C=\frac{6\theta}{7}\).

Using \(\frac{\sin A+\sin C}{\cos A+\cos C}=\tan B\):
\[\frac{\sin\frac{5\theta}{7}+\sin\frac{6\theta}{7}}{\cos\frac{5\theta}{7}+\cos\frac{6\theta}{7}}=\tan\frac{11\theta}{14}=\sqrt3.\]
\[\frac{11\theta}{14}=\frac\pi3,\frac{4\pi}3\]
\[\theta=\frac{14\pi}{33},\frac{56\pi}{33}.\]
